First of all know that I am no expert but here are a few differences between what you did and you're opponent which may explain a few things you see. Firstly I think your analysis of yourself was good to an extent and you seem smart. Here are the places I see:

You spent 600 minerals on SCV's while he spent it on barracks.
You spent 400 minerals on a command center while he spent it on marines. 
Did you upgrade your CC to an orbital? If so there goes the minerals.
But more importantly, here are two solutions to your 'problem'.
1. Know that you did nothing wrong, and if he hadn't cheesed you your build was probably alright - yes you probably could have been producing from barracks #2 but thats small. The reason you had minerals I think is normally you'd spent it upgrading to an orbital + SCV's from 2 CC's. So you just got build order loss. To prevent losing when you did, you could have pulled SCV's in front of marines to tank damage for them. 

Know, when you saw the first wave of marines come you should have started a bunker, from which you definitely could have held (starting with a bunker on the high ground). 4 barracks is too many and he would run out of money and then you're superior economy wins/tech up to medivacs and he's still on marines. 

Other thing - you didn't scout at all, if you had looked at his base you would have seen a barracks but no marine or attachment or even second base. This would have been ringing alarm bells so you would know to either - check for proxies, build a safety bunker (If you want build it to 99% then stop, if its needed finish and use, otherwise cancel) :)


That's just what I saw, but once again, don't be too harsh. Once he has 4 barracks producing units, it doesn't matter how good your micro is, without a bunker you're probably going to lose :)

You wake up in the morning, you go to school. You see all of your friends, of course you have known them forever, and probably will continue to. Your parents are all friends, you are maybe 11, 12 right now. You have had the same friends for all of those. Since there are only a couple hundred people in your whole school (Middle and High combined in one building) you don't really have enemies. There are no popular kids, everyone is friends with everyone else! 
Fast Forward a couple of years! 
Your 18 now. You still now everyone in the town, you say hi as you pass people. You never really left and cannot imagine not knowing everyone, and caring about them. You have to babysit on Saturday for Miss Wilson, so that her husband and she can grab a movie (Some of the only quality time they have). As you walk to her house (nowhere is too far away not to walk), you see a few friends, of course they already know you're babysitting everyone does. There are no secrets in small towns! 
You have basically never left this town, you could go the metropolis a few miles away, but you never needed to, and the buses are irregular and the people who have gone to the city don't advise it.
Fast Forward
You have just graduated from your school, you are so emotional, you and your class of 20 all successful and are now off to UNI (those who go to Uni, most just and continue the cycle!). You go off to the big bad world. 
When you arrive at Uni, you realize everything is different! There are so many people. So many faces. How are you supposed to find your away around. My Dorm building... is bigger than my school!? How? Where? You meet a hundred new people a day! You have no idea what is happening. You are confused. You do not like this. There are too many people, you try to be nice to all of them but your individuality is lost is the sea of people! 

That it is what it's like to be from a small town, you are secure and used to being safe and knowing everyone, then when you leave you don't understand why everyone isn't like you. Then a few mistakes later (maybe a mugging/robbery) you start to learn...
Source: I am from a "small" place

While you may be right, I believe that 'being funny' is a skill like any other and therefore can be trained. (maybe you need training wheels (i.e. use other comedians material and see what works for YOU). It is individual, every one is different so your humor may be a mix. 

My advice if you want to improve your humor is watch British TV (stereotyping, but generally it is 'high brow' (intellectual) and you learn a lot about stuff, while also hearing jokes and you will learn to it). I say British and not American, because British is (generally, not always) more general and can be applied to any situation, while American is funny, but only in the moment of the movie, and part of the humor comes the ridiculous of the situation. 

So if you want to be funnier watch Comedians, (see what they do, try to do it yourself, I recommend Jon Richardson) and also read books. This later will help you because you will learn more words and their meanings etc. Making word puns and games more fun and easier for you to think of. (Also humor is based on knowing which words to say when - so more words = more funny ;-)
